subject: Post-call: MedTect inference deep-dive — latency / throughput SLOs & deployment options
messages:

Subject: Post-call: MedTect inference deep-dive — latency / throughput SLOs & deployment options

Hi Anya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we've got a shared view and clear next steps. Short version first, details below.

Summary of what we heard today (pain / goals):
- Primary pain: inconsistent latency under peak (user-facing inference can spike p95 to ~450–600ms for ~400–600 token prompts).
- Business goal: sub-350ms p95 at 95% of traffic; sustained throughput target of ~120–150 reqs/s during business hours (spikes to 220 RPS).
- Reg/Compliance: PHI in some payloads — customer requires private deployment / VPC option and SOC 2 evidence.
- Models: currently evaluating 70B instruction-tuned models; willing to try quantized variants (q4/q5) but want quality checks.
- Data residency: US-only; low tolerance for cross-region failover unless encrypted and logged.

Technical constraints/notes we captured:
- Representative prompt size: 350–600 tokens (avg 420) with a long context window for retrieval-augmented generation.
- KV cache reuse expected for conversational flows (we should leverage prefix/KV caching to avoid repeated compute on long contexts).
- Payload sizes with embeddings and RAG layers: additional network egress during retrieval — will affect end-to-end latency.

Suggested POC scope (proposed):
1) Topology options: Private (customer-controlled VPC) vs Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud) — we'll map performance/cost for both.
2) Model variants: run 70B q4_0 (or q5), plus a smaller 13B instruction model for degraded-path fallback.
3) Runtime optimizations: KV caching, batching (micro-batch 8–16), and optimized kernels for 512+ token sequences.
4) Success criteria: achieve p95 <= 350ms on a sustained 120 RPS synthetic workload matching your production prompt distribution; produce quality parity report vs current baseline.

Immediate next steps / asks from MedTect:
- Please share a sanitized sample set of 20 representative prompts and an example payload with typical context (Anya mentioned you would attach in follow-up).
- Confirm procurement contact (you mentioned procurement@medtect.com).
- Confirm any additional compliance evidence requests beyond SOC 2 that we should prepare.

What we'll deliver (internal owners):
- Detailed topology + sizing options (Marissa) — target delivery: 3 business days.
- Cost and latency estimate for both Dedicated and Private options (Laura) — target delivery: EOD Friday.
- SOC2 evidence and security worksheet (Karthik) — target: attachment / link in 5 business days.

Attachments referenced: please attach sample prompts (if possible). I will attach an initial PoC scoping sheet and a one-page topology summary in my next mail.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical kickoff next week (Sept 15–17). What's your availability?

Thanks — looking forward to running the POC and proving the performance.

—

Couple of technical notes to help shape the topology doc: 

- For a 70B instruction model (quantized q4_0/q5), realistic starting topology for target 120–150 RPS with p95 <= 350ms: Dedicated cluster with 8x A100-80GB (or equivalent H100 pool) using sharded serving and contiguous KV cache. That assumes micro-batching at 8 and aggressive KV reuse.
- Private/VPC option will add ~20–50ms network overhead depending on cross-VPC nat/firewall rules and RAG retrieval service placement — we should colocate retrieval and Redis/KV in the same VPC to keep TTFB minimal.
- Fallback plan: route 10–15% of tail traffic to a smaller 13B model (single-node) when queued latency exceeds threshold; this keeps user experience reasonable and reduces cost on spikes.
- Measurement hooks: we should instrument token-level latency (service, model, retrieval, network) and export traces to your observability (or ours temporarily) so we can tune batching and prefetch parameters.

I'll draft the topology options with explicit GPU counts, expected RPS per pod, and a short runbook for POC tuning. Marissa — putting this on your radar to merge into the customer-facing PDF.
